correctness.rationale: For weakly increasing full chain maps n>=1 of image rank r, the double-simplex proof is valid. Convexity of prefix-sum work over the multiplicity simplex and convexity of absolute displacement over the image-gap simplex reduce the problem to (r)(r+1) vertices, each with work N(N+1)/2+N d_{mk}. The only maximum vertex pairs for r>=2 are (1,r) and (r,0); positivity of product weights forces the stated two endpoint-compressed maps. For r=1 strictly maximal constant maps are the two endpoints; for r=n the identity is sole possibility. The explicitly weighted nonnegative deficit certificate follows by subtracting Jensen bounds. A separate fresh exhaustive enumerator checked 33,098 weakly monotone maps through n=9, their ranks, exact maximizers, and rational stability remainders.
residual_risks: Finite n<=9 exhaustive calculation only corroborates, not proves all n; universal conclusion rests on the two convexity arguments and equality-support argument.
